summary: Low-disruption structural additions that make the SpendCube v2 codebase capable of supporting full procurement analytics across direct and indirect spend. Six targeted stories: (1) SQL schema extension with analytics-critical fields and new reference tables; (2) new analytical query endpoints on the FastAPI backend; (3) extended TypeScript types with a flexible Category tree and expanded FilterState; (4) global filter context and shared aggregation utilities; (5) expanded FilterBar and drilldown navigation pattern; (6) Python pipeline updates to populate new fields. No existing pages or APIs are removed or broken. All changes are purely additive.

decisions.additive_only: All changes are additive. No existing columns, endpoints, pages, or tests are removed or modified. The goal is to unblock future analytics work without rework.
decisions.category_type_dual_approach: CategoryRow (the existing l1/l2/l3 flat type) is kept for backward compatibility with existing pages. A new flexible Category interface (category_id, parent_category_id, category_level, category_name) is added alongside it. Existing pages continue using CategoryRow. New pages will use Category.
decisions.filter_context_migration: FilterState moves from local useState in each page to a React Context (FilterContext.tsx). The existing useFilters hook is refactored to be a thin wrapper over useContext(FilterContext) so existing pages require no changes — they call useFilters() exactly as before.
decisions.abc_segmentation: ABC segmentation follows the Pareto convention: A = suppliers contributing to top 80% of spend; B = next 15%; C = bottom 5%. Computed server-side in the /cube/abc-analysis endpoint from the transactions view. The abc_segment TEXT column on transactions is populated by the cube builder pipeline step.
decisions.new_tables_nullable_fk: The new reference tables (categories, legal_entities, payment_term_mappings) use nullable foreign keys — transactions.legal_entity is a TEXT code that may or may not match a legal_entities row. This avoids migration complexity and lets the tables be populated incrementally.
decisions.python_fields_nullable: New fields added to CanonicalTransaction (legal_entity, vendor_country, plant_country, categorisation_status, abc_segment, manual_override_flag, ai_classification_flag) are all Optional with None defaults. Existing ingestion logic is unchanged; fields are populated where source data provides them.

existing_tables.transactions: 45-column table. MISSING: legal_entity, vendor_country, plant_country, categorisation_status, manual_override_flag, ai_classification_flag, harmonised_payment_term, discount_percent, discount_days, has_early_payment_discount, payment_term_confidence, abc_segment. All 12 will be added as nullable TEXT/INTEGER/DOUBLE PRECISION columns in migration 002.
existing_tables.supplier_master: Existing 8 columns + engagement_id. No changes needed — harmonisation_status and harmonisation_method are already captured in supplier_match_log.match_method and review_status.
existing_tables.categories_new: NEW table: flexible taxonomy tree. id UUID, engagement_id UUID, category_id TEXT, parent_category_id TEXT, category_level INTEGER, category_name TEXT, taxonomy_version TEXT DEFAULT 'v1', is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ. Supports arbitrary depth (L1–L5+).
existing_tables.legal_entities_new: NEW table: id UUID, engagement_id UUID, legal_entity_code TEXT, legal_entity_name TEXT, country TEXT, currency TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
existing_tables.payment_term_mappings_new: NEW table: id UUID, engagement_id UUID, raw_payment_term TEXT, harmonised_payment_term TEXT, payment_term_days INTEGER, discount_percent DOUBLE PRECISION DEFAULT 0, discount_days INTEGER DEFAULT 0, has_early_payment_discount BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, confidence_score DOUBLE PRECISION, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.

userStories.title: SQL schema extension — analytics fields, reference tables, and new views
userStories.description: Add the 12 analytics-critical columns missing from the transactions table, create three new reference tables (categories, legal_entities, payment_term_mappings), and add four new aggregation views (v_by_legal_entity, v_by_currency, v_by_country, v_abc_analysis). This migration is purely additive — all new columns are nullable and the existing 001 migration is not modified.
acceptanceCriteria: Create file: supabase/migrations/002_analytics_extensions.sql

Migration adds to transactions table (all nullable): ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS legal_entity TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS vendor_country TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS plant_country TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS categorisation_status TEXT DEFAULT 'uncategorised'; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS manual_override_flag INTEGER DEFAULT 0; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ai_classification_flag INTEGER DEFAULT 0; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS harmonised_payment_term TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS discount_percent DOUBLE PRECISION DEFAULT 0; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS discount_days INTEGER DEFAULT 0; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS has_early_payment_discount INTEGER DEFAULT 0; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS payment_term_confidence DOUBLE PRECISION; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS abc_segment TEXT

Migration creates table categories: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, category_id TEXT NOT NULL, parent_category_id TEXT, category_level INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, category_name TEXT NOT NULL, taxonomy_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'v1', is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true, mapping_confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, mapping_source TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(). UNIQUE(engagement_id, category_id, taxonomy_version).

Migration creates table legal_entities: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, legal_entity_code TEXT NOT NULL, legal_entity_name TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT, currency TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(). UNIQUE(engagement_id, legal_entity_code).

Migration creates table payment_term_mappings: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, raw_payment_term TEXT NOT NULL, harmonised_payment_term TEXT, payment_term_days INTEGER, discount_percent DOUBLE PRECISION DEFAULT 0, discount_days INTEGER DEFAULT 0, has_early_payment_discount BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, confidence_score DOUBLE PRECISION, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(). UNIQUE(engagement_id, raw_payment_term).

Migration creates indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_transactions_legal_entity ON transactions(engagement_id, legal_entity); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_transactions_vendor_country ON transactions(engagement_id, vendor_country); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_transactions_abc_segment ON transactions(engagement_id, abc_segment); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_transactions_cat_status ON transactions(engagement_id, categorisation_status)

Migration creates view v_by_legal_entity: SELECT engagement_id, legal_entity, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(DISTINCT canonical_supplier_id) AS supplier_count, COUNT(DISTINCT category_l1) AS category_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 AND legal_entity IS NOT NULL GROUP BY engagement_id, legal_entity

Migration creates view v_by_currency: SELECT engagement_id, original_currency AS currency, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend_base, SUM(original_amount) AS total_spend_original, COUNT(DISTINCT canonical_supplier_id) AS supplier_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, original_currency

Migration creates view v_by_country: SELECT engagement_id, vendor_country AS country, 'vendor' AS country_type, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(DISTINCT canonical_supplier_id) AS supplier_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 AND vendor_country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY engagement_id, vendor_country

Migration creates view v_abc_analysis: SELECT engagement_id, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(SUM(base_amount)) OVER (PARTITION BY engagement_id ORDER BY SUM(base_amount) DESC) AS cumulative_spend, SUM(SUM(base_amount)) OVER (PARTITION BY engagement_id) AS grand_total FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name

Migration enables RLS on new tables: ALTER TABLE categories ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE legal_entities ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE payment_term_mappings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY

Migration creates RLS SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on categories, legal_entities, payment_term_mappings using same pattern as 001: engagement_id IN (SELECT id FROM engagements WHERE owner_email = auth.jwt()->>'email')
Verify: SQL file is valid (no syntax errors detectable by review). File must be self-contained with IF NOT EXISTS guards so it is safe to re-run.

userStories.title: Backend — five new analytical cube endpoints
userStories.description: Add five new GET endpoints to backend/app/routers/cube.py that query the new views and compute analytics not available in the existing endpoints. All endpoints follow the exact same pattern as existing cube endpoints (engagement ownership check, SQLAlchemy text query, typed response). No existing endpoints are modified.

GET /api/engagements/{engagement_id}/cube/by-legal-entity — SELECT from v_by_legal_entity WHERE engagement_id=? ORDER BY total_spend DESC; returns list of {legal_entity, transaction_count, total_spend, supplier_count, category_count}

GET /api/engagements/{engagement_id}/cube/by-currency — SELECT from v_by_currency WHERE engagement_id=? ORDER BY total_spend_base DESC; returns list of {currency, transaction_count, total_spend_base, total_spend_original, supplier_count}

GET /api/engagements/{engagement_id}/cube/by-country — SELECT from v_by_country WHERE engagement_id=? ORDER BY total_spend DESC; returns list of {country, country_type, transaction_count, total_spend, supplier_count}

GET /api/engagements/{engagement_id}/cube/abc-analysis — SELECT from v_abc_analysis WHERE engagement_id=? ORDER BY total_spend DESC; computes abc_segment in Python: A if cumulative_spend/grand_total <= 0.80 else B if <= 0.95 else C; returns list of {canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, total_spend, transaction_count, cumulative_spend_pct, abc_segment}

All 5 endpoints support the standard filter query params: date_from, date_to (passed as WHERE invoice_date BETWEEN filters)

userStories.title: Global filter context, shared aggregation utilities, and drilldown hook
userStories.description: Three pure-addition files that provide the architectural foundation for all future analytics pages: (1) FilterContext.tsx moves filter state to React Context so it persists across page navigation; (2) aggregations.ts provides reusable metric calculations (ABC, concentration, tail spend, top-N) that pages import instead of reinventing; (3) useDrilldown.ts manages the overview→category→supplier→transaction navigation pattern with a DrilldownBreadcrumb component. risks: categoriser.py edit (US-006): The categorisation_status update must happen after the final category is written to the transactions table, not before. Check the write order in categoriser.py — if it uses batch inserts, add a post-insert UPDATE step rather than modifying the insert.

cube/pipeline.py ABC computation (US-006): The ABC UPDATE loop touches every transaction row for the engagement. For large datasets this can be slow. Use a single UPDATE transactions SET abc_segment = CASE ... with a subquery rather than a Python loop over individual rows.

FilterContext URL init (US-004): Reading filter state from URL search params on init can cause hydration issues in Vite dev mode if the URL params include arrays (e.g. legal_entities=A&legal_entities=B). Use URLSearchParams.getAll() not .get() for array fields.

v_abc_analysis window function (US-001): The SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY engagement_id ORDER BY ...) window function requires Postgres 8.4+. Supabase uses Postgres 15+ so this is safe, but verify the view definition doesn't reference engagement_id in both the GROUP BY and window function ambiguously.
